ko_summary: @patrick_oshag가 누뱅크 다비드 벨레스를 인용했다: 심각한 재정 상황으로 세계 약 190개 통화가 10~20년 안에 10개로 줄 수 있고 스테이블코인이 달러를 구할 수 있다.
text:
David Vélez on why stablecoins could save the US dollar:

"There are about 190 currencies around the world. My view is that in 10-20 years from now, those 190 will be 10.

The fiscal situation in so many countries around the world is so dire that a lot of that fiat money is not real money. 

And so increasingly, billions of people are going to be banking on the offshore world, US stablecoin, but also Bitcoin and other type of assets.

I think the US stablecoins ultimately will be the big savior or one of the biggest saviors of the US dollar, because it democratizes access to the US dollar.

At least there is a lot of demand for the US stablecoin. There's very little for the Brazilian stablecoin, unfortunately."

Elon commenting yikes because $CRWV is primary competitor to $SPCX. Truth: vast majority of $CRWV capital structure is secured contract-backed facilities priced off offtake quality and GPU collateral. Only ~10% unsecured that might trade at 15%. These 15% yields alarm for future unsecured but focused on mid single digit contract-backed loans, not major red flag to the buildout.
ko_summary: 좋아하는 AI 주식들이 7월 이후 보지 못한 수준으로 매우 안 좋은 하루. 공포를 만드는 이들의 인센티브를 이해하는 것이 중요. Chamath 게시물은 유료 기사로 연결. Elon이 yikes라고 한 것은 $CRWV가 $SPCX의 주요 경쟁자이기 때문. 진실: $CRWV 자본 구조의 대다수는 고객 오프테이크 품질과 GPU 담보로 가격이 책정된 담보 계약 기반 시설. 약 10%만 무담보로 15%에 거래될 수 있음. 이 15% 수익률은 미래 무담보 채권에 경보지만 중단위 계약 기반 대출에 집중하므로 빌드아웃의 주요 레드 플래그는 아님.
text:
Really nasty day for our favorite AI stocks with levels unseen since July.

It's important to 1) understand the incentives of those creating the fear and 2) not take tweets at face value without doing your own research.

Chamath made this post because it links to a paywalled article and the attention lands right in his pocket. Elon commenting "yikes" because $CRWV is a primary competitor to $SPCX, and it's a chance for a cheap dig.

The truth: The vast majority of $CRWV's capital structure is secured, contract-backed facilities that are priced off customer offtake quality and GPU collateral. Only around 10% of their debt is the unsecured stuff that might trade at 15% if they seek more...

These 15% yields are alarming showing what $CRWV would have to pay for future unsecured bonds they issue but given they're focused on these contract-backed loans that have come in at mid single digits I don't really see this as some major red flag to the buildout.

en_summary: KawzInvests analyzes $CRWV Q2 10-Q, noting only 4% of ~$35B debt is at 15% ($1.3B loan due March 2028 being paid down). Actual blended interest ~8.4% including convertibles at ~2% and bonds at 9-10%. Main funding via customer-contract loans, e.g. Meta-backed at ~5.9%. AI trade intact; $ASML reported record Q3 profit, lithography demand outruns supply into 2027-28 even with +30% capacity/year, customers asking for 2029-30 slots. Demand outpaces supply. $CRWV $ASML
ko_summary: KawzInvests가 $CRWV Q2 10-Q를 분석, 약 350억 달러 부채 중 4%만 15% 금리($13억 대출, 2028년 3월 만기, 상환 중)라고 지적. 실제 혼합 금리는 약 8.4%로 전환사채 약 2%, 채권 9-10% 포함. 주요 자금은 고객 계약 대출, 예: Meta 지원 약 5.9%. AI 거래는 여전히 온전하다; $ASML 기록적 Q3 이익 보고, 리소그래피 수요가 연간 +30% 용량에도 2027-28년 공급 초과, 고객이 2029-30 슬롯 문의. 수요가 공급을 앞지름. $CRWV $ASML
text:
$CRWV isn’t paying 15% interest. Only 4% of their debt costs that.

I went through the Q2 10-Q line by line. Out of ~$35B in debt, exactly one loan sits at 15%. It’s $1.3B, due March 2028, and already being paid down.

The 15% chart going around is the market yield on their 2032 bond. A higher yield doesn’t change what CoreWeave pays. It works like a mortgage. If you locked in at 3% and rates go to 7%, you’re still paying 3%. CoreWeave locked that bond at 9.625% and still pays 9.625%.

What they actually pay

> $6.6B of convertibles at ~2%
> ~$10B of bonds at 9-10%
> Most secured loans around 9%
> ~8.4% blended across everything

They have roughly $20B of 2026 capex left to fund, and 2027 will need more. Their main funding tool has been loans backed by customer contracts. The investment grade one backed by Meta priced around 5.9% in March. If they keep borrowing that way, I think the math holds.

Zooming out, the AI trade still looks intact to me. $ASML reported record Q3 profit this morning and said lithography demand will outrun their supply in 2027 and 2028, even after adding ~30% capacity each year. Customers are already asking about 2029 and 2030 slots. 

Demand is still outpacing supply everywhere I look. $CRWV $ASML

text:
MIDDLE EAST OIL FLOWS: Despite a wave of Iranian attacks since the beginning of October, total Middle Eastern crude oil flows (ex-Iran) remain resilient. Flows are becoming, however, lumpier (days of multiple tanker crossings followed by days of very few tankers). 

Overall, Middle East (ex-Iran) crude flows, including Strait of Hormuz plus all the bypass routes, are holding at ~75% of pre-war levels, down from a ~95% *peak* in the last days of September. Crucially, despite the drop in recent days, the Oct 1-Oct 10 period average remains above Sep full month average (and well above full month August). Kuwait is struggling the most right now. UAE, Iraq and KSA (the last one using both Persian Gulf and Red Sea) are doing relatively well.

All said, the risk is to the downside if the Iranian attacks continue (and if they become more successful). Iran has sunk at least one container ship in the SoH over the last 24 hours. The same goes for Red Sea flows under Houthi / Iraq militias potential attacks. For Iran itself, Hormuz remains closed.

One key indicator to follow: despite the Iranian attacks against SoH traffic, the physical premium for Middle Eastern crude has come down significantly in recent days, touching today a near 2½-month low.

zh_summary: @Greenbackd：股市是預測機器，反映多年的盈利預期，因此當前景不再惡化時，即使現況仍差，股價也可能急轉。
en_summary: @Greenbackd: the stock market is a forecasting machine pricing profits over many years, so when the outlook stops deteriorating prices can turn sharply even while conditions remain dire.
ko_summary: @Greenbackd: 주식시장은 수년간의 이익을 반영하는 예측 기계라 전망 악화가 멈추면 현재 상황이 나빠도 주가는 급반전할 수 있다.
text:
The stock market is a forecasting machine. Prices reflect what investors collectively expect profits to be over many years, not what the economy is doing today.
When the outlook stops deteriorating, even while current conditions remain dire, prices can turn sharply higher.
The clearest evidence is the gap between the market’s low and the worst point for jobs.
In every recession since 1970, the stock market bottomed before unemployment peaked. The typical lead was about seven months. In 1990–92, the market had been recovering for nearly two years before the jobless rate topped out.

zh_summary: @cullenroche：長期國債是唯一能提供實質收益並在崩盤時傾向上漲的資產，但主要只在通縮或增長恐慌（如2008年）時有效，且多數時間實質價值在流失。價外認沽期權是真正的崩盤保險，但持有有成本。長存續期資產中的「安全收益」近乎神話；派息必需消費品最接近，而分派收益和緩衝收益基金多屬行銷噱頭。
en_summary: @cullenroche: long Treasuries are the only asset paying real income that tends to rally in a crash, but mainly in deflationary or growth scares like 2008, and they bleed in real terms most of the time. OTM puts are true crash insurance but cost money to hold. Safe income in long duration assets is a myth; dividend paying consumer staples come closest, while distribution yield and buffered income funds are mostly marketing.
ko_summary: @cullenroche: 장기 국채는 실질 소득을 주면서 폭락 때 오르는 유일한 자산이지만 2008년 같은 디플레이션이나 성장 공포에서만 주로 통하고 대부분 실질 가치가 깎인다. 외가격 풋은 진짜 폭락 보험이지만 보유 비용이 든다. 장기 듀레이션 자산의 안전한 소득은 환상에 가깝고, 배당 필수소비재가 가장 가깝다. 분배수익률 펀드와 버퍼형 인컴 상품은 대부분 마케팅이다.
text:
Tough question. Income with crash hedging but not stocks, credit or MF? Long Treasuries are the only thing that pays you real income and tends to rally in a crash. The catch is they only work in a deflationary or growth scare like 2008. That's the plain vanilla tail hedge with income, but long bonds are terrible long duration assets to hold because they bleed in real terms most of the time. 

OTM puts are true crash insurance in any environment, but they cost you money to wait. 

Frankly, I think the idea of "safe" income in a long duration asset is a bit like turning water into wine. Lots of products claim to provide it, but there are huge trade-offs in the long run so I'd personally treat income as safe income and long duration hedgers as something different. Dividend paying consumer staples might be as close as you can get to the holy grail of equity+income (but even those are paying out of tax efficient capital). These popular distribution yield funds and all the income buffered stuff are good marketing materials, but mostly counterproductive compared to something like home grown dividend strategies....

en_summary: @aleabitoreddit says $AGLT (Agility Robotics) has cleared SEC review for public listing through $CCXI. Estimated timeline: about Oct 13 S-4 effective, about Nov 2 shareholder vote, merger close and ticker live in November 2026. Company expects close in November 2026 subject to Churchill XI shareholder approval.
ko_summary: @aleabitoreddit는 $AGLT(Agility Robotics)가 $CCXI를 통한 상장 SEC 심사를 통과했다고 했다. 대략 10/13 S-4 효력, 11/2 주주투표, 2026년 11월 합병·티커 거래 개시 일정이며, Churchill XI 주주 승인 등 조건 하에 2026년 11월 종결 예정이다.
text:
$AGLT (Agility Robotics) has cleared SEC review for public listing through $CCXI

If you want an estimate timeline:

~Oct 13 (today): SEC S-4 declared effective

~Nov 2nd (shareholder vote): for merger approval

~November: Merger closing and ticker goes live for trading. 

Company’s official statement was:

“The business combination remains subject to approval by Churchill XI shareholders and other customary closing conditions, and is expected to close in November 2026.”

So likely less than a month away for the first pure play US humanoid company to go live!
